userStories.title: Advertise REVIEW and FIX in assistant and MCP dispatch catalogs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the koda_dispatch_job descriptor and its assistant/MCP descriptions to advertise the existing PR commands.

**Motivation** — Today an agent in a koda thread or over MCP cannot ask for a review or a fix (the tool's `command` enum is `RUN` and `PLAN`), a CLI user cannot either (`--feature` is required and there is no PR flag), and a person reading a finished review on the web has no way to act on it except by hand.

**Approach** — Assistant tool descriptor. `koda_dispatch_job`'s descriptor `command` enum becomes `['RUN', 'PLAN', 'REVIEW', 'FIX']`, it gains an optional `prNumber` property (`type: 'integer'`, `minimum: 1`, `maximum: 2147483647`) and `required` becomes `['repo', 'command', 'maxCostUsd']`. The catalog description names `REVIEW` (review an open pull request) and `FIX` (review then fix an open pull request) and says they take `prNumber` instead of `feature`; it keeps its "only after the user approves" and "do not call this tool again" sentences and stays within the 2000-character cap with the workspace sentence appended. `MCP_DESCRIPTIONS.koda_dispatch_job` names the same three terms and keeps its run-at-once sentence and `MCP_PROJECT_SENTENCE`. Neither side validates the schema itself (MCP delegates validation to the executor; the runner's assign parser checks only that `inputSchema` is an object), so the new property and `required` list need no other change.

Update the existing descriptor spec's AC-8 required list and AC-9 command enum, and extend its bounds assertion with prNumber; every other assertion stays. Add the dedicated PR descriptor spec, using the MCP catalog's existing by-name lookup and workspace projection patterns.

**Scope** — In: KODA_DISPATCH_JOB schema, assistant wording, MCP wording and descriptor regression anchors. Out: parser changes (US-002), preview/execute/approval integration (US-003), and runner/MCP schema-validation changes.

**Interface** — `KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema.properties.command.enum = ['RUN', 'PLAN', 'REVIEW', 'FIX']`; `prNumber: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 2147483647 }`; `required: ['repo', 'command', 'maxCostUsd']`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema property command has enum ['RUN', 'PLAN', 'REVIEW', 'FIX'].
[unit] KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema property prNumber matches { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 2147483647 }.
[unit] KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema.required equals ['repo', 'command', 'maxCostUsd'].
[unit] KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.description mentions each of REVIEW, FIX and prNumber.
[unit] The description kodaToolDescriptorsFor('WORKSPACE') gives koda_dispatch_job is at most 2000 characters long.
[unit] The MCP tool catalog's description of koda_dispatch_job mentions each of REVIEW, FIX and prNumber.
[unit] The MCP tool catalog's description of koda_dispatch_job ends with the MCP project sentence naming the project argument.

[unit] KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.description retains 'The job is started only after the user approves it: this call proposes it and the user decides it, so tell the user it is waiting for their approval and do not call this tool again for the same job.', preserving the existing thread approval wording.
[unit] The MCP tool catalog's description of koda_dispatch_job retains 'The call runs at once as the calling agent', preserving the existing immediate-execution wording.

routing.reasoning: Bounded catalog and description changes across two existing modules; approval policy and access enforcement remain untouched.

modifiedFiles.reason: `KODA_DISPATCH_JOB` command enum gains `REVIEW` and `FIX`, gains the `prNumber` integer property, `required` drops `feature`, and its description names REVIEW, FIX and `prNumber` while keeping its approval and do-not-call-again sentences.

AC-8 (`required` equals `['repo', 'command', 'feature', 'maxCostUsd']`) becomes `['repo', 'command', 'maxCostUsd']`, and AC-9 (`command` enum equals `['RUN', 'PLAN']`) becomes `['RUN', 'PLAN', 'REVIEW', 'FIX']`; the bounds test gains `prNumber` as `{ type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 2147483647 }`. Every other assertion stays.
`MCP_DESCRIPTIONS.koda_dispatch_job` names REVIEW, FIX and `prNumber`; it keeps the run-at-once sentence and `MCP_PROJECT_SENTENCE`.

userStories.title: Parse assistant REVIEW and FIX dispatch input
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend dispatchJobTool's input union and parser to accept PR commands without changing RUN/PLAN parsing.

**Motivation** — K3-A shipped the `FIX` job kind and K3-B1 (PR #365) the follow-up review after a pushed fix, both live-checked (§9.155, §9.156) only through `curl` against the REST route.

**Approach** — The tool's `COMMANDS` list becomes `['RUN', 'PLAN', 'REVIEW', 'FIX']`. `DispatchJobInput` becomes `command: 'RUN' | 'PLAN' | 'REVIEW' | 'FIX'`, `feature?: string`, `prNumber?: number`. `parse` keeps every existing check and adds: for `RUN` and `PLAN` a missing `feature` refuses with reason `feature` (the existing rule, now conditional); a present `feature` on any command keeps its existing string bounds (reason `feature`); for `REVIEW` and `FIX` a missing `prNumber` refuses with reason `prNumber`; a present `prNumber` on any command that is not an integer from 1 to 2147483647 refuses with reason `prNumber`. Cross-field refusals (a `feature` on `FIX`, a `prNumber` on `RUN`, a `ref` on `REVIEW`) are left to `normalizeDispatch` in `preview`, which already turns its reason into a `ToolInputError`.

Keep repo, maxCostUsd, ref, planFrom, profiles, bashMode and ticketRefs checks and omission of absent optional properties unchanged. The RUN/PLAN parse results are unchanged, so every assertion in the existing tool spec keeps holding. Copy the existing harness, VALID fixture and reasonOf pattern into the new parser spec.

**Scope** — In: COMMANDS, DispatchJobInput, parse and parser behavior tests. Out: descriptor wording (US-001), GitHub preview refusal, preview text, DTO mapping and approval-route integration (US-003).

**Interface** — `command: 'RUN' | 'PLAN' | 'REVIEW' | 'FIX'`, `feature?: string`, `prNumber?: number` on `DispatchJobInput`; `parse(input: unknown): DispatchJobInput`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parse({ repo: 'acme/app', command: 'FIX', prNumber: 23, maxCostUsd: 1 }) returns { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'FIX', prNumber: 23, maxCostUsd: 1 }.
[unit] Table-driven: parse with command REVIEW and prNumber absent, 0, 1.5, '23' or 2147483648 throws ToolInputError with reason prNumber.
[unit] parse with command RUN, a valid feature and prNumber 0 throws ToolInputError with reason prNumber.
[unit] parse with command PLAN and no feature throws ToolInputError with reason feature.
[unit] parse with command FIX, prNumber 23 and a feature of 129 characters throws ToolInputError with reason feature.

[unit] parse({ repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5 }) returns exactly { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5 }, preserving the existing RUN parse result and omission of absent optional fields.

[unit] parse({ repo: 'acme/app', command: 'PLAN', feature: 'add-auth', planFrom: 'docs/spec.md', maxCostUsd: 0.5 }) returns exactly { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'PLAN', feature: 'add-auth', planFrom: 'docs/spec.md', maxCostUsd: 0.5 }, preserving the existing PLAN parse result.
[unit] Table-driven: parse with command FIX and prNumber absent, 0, 1.5, '23' or 2147483648 throws ToolInputError with reason prNumber.
[unit] parse with command RUN and no feature throws ToolInputError with reason feature, preserving the existing missing-feature refusal.

routing.reasoning: One existing parser and input interface gain bounded optional data; cross-field and authorization policy stay downstream.

modifiedFiles.reason: `COMMANDS` and `DispatchJobInput` gain `REVIEW`/`FIX` and `prNumber`, `feature` becomes optional, and `parse` gains the rules of call 4; the RUN/PLAN parse results are unchanged, so every assertion in the existing tool spec keeps holding.

userStories.title: Preview and dispatch approved assistant PR jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preview REVIEW/FIX requests before approval and dispatch the existing PR DTO as the approving workflow's requester.

**Motivation** — The K3 design goal 1 says a `FIX` can be dispatched "from REST, CLI, MCP and web (agent-first: no surface special-cased)", and §D7 notes K1 shipped `REVIEW` without a CLI flag.

**Approach** — Cross-field refusals (a `feature` on `FIX`, a `prNumber` on `RUN`, a `ref` on `REVIEW`) are left to `normalizeDispatch` in `preview`, which already turns its reason into a `ToolInputError`. Before that, `preview` refuses a `REVIEW` or `FIX` on a repo whose `provider` is not `github` with `ToolInputError` reason `review is GitHub-only` or `fix is GitHub-only` (the service's own wording), so the user is never asked to approve a dispatch that would be refused. `preview` for `REVIEW` and `FIX` answers `Dispatch <command> in <slug>:`, then `repo: <owner>/<name> @ <defaultBranch>`, then `pull request: #<prNumber>`, then `max cost: $<maxCostUsd>`, then one `profiles:` line when profiles are given; the `RUN`/`PLAN` preview is unchanged. `toDto` carries `prNumber` when present and `feature` only when present.

`normalizeDispatch(dto, defaultBranch)` for `REVIEW`/`FIX` refuses a missing `prNumber` (`prNumber required for <command>`), a `feature` (`feature is derived for <command>`), a `planFrom`, a `ref`, a non-`raw` `bashMode` and `ticketRefs`; for `RUN`/`PLAN` refuses a `prNumber` (`prNumber is only for REVIEW and FIX`). Keep this server function unchanged. Preserve fleetWriteRefusal, maskSecrets, jobPath, project-scoped repository resolution, re-resolution on execute, and existing actor identity. The RUN/PLAN preview and DTO are unchanged, so every assertion in the existing tool spec keeps holding.

Add unit tests in dispatch-job-tool.pr.spec.ts and an integration test through the real runner tool route and the approval decide route `POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions`, in a new file that copies the harness of `assistant-dispatch-job-tool.integration.spec.ts` (copy the helpers it uses). The test uses pull request number 7023, so its feature `review-pr-7023` is used by no other spec (`.nax/rules/api-test-isolation.md`). Enter `POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_dispatch_job?leaseEpoch=1` using the runner holding the THREAD job, inspect the stored action preview, then approve through the engine route and inspect actual FleetJob rows. Keep the shared DB gate, environment restoration and app teardown; run the real-DB test outside the sandbox.

**Scope** — In: GitHub-only preview refusal, PR preview lines, optional DTO fields, and the runner/proposal/approval/persisted-job seam. Out: parser implementation (US-002), catalog descriptions (US-001), API route/DTO/permission/approval policy/audit changes, CLI and web surfaces.

**Interface** — `preview(ctx: ToolContext, input: DispatchJobInput): Promise<string>`; `execute(ctx: ToolContext, input: DispatchJobInput): Promise<string>`; `toDto(input: DispatchJobInput, repoId: string): DispatchFleetJobDto`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] preview for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'FIX', prNumber: 23, maxCostUsd: 1, profiles: ['native-codex'] } in project web with the repo's default branch main returns the lines 'Dispatch FIX in web:', 'repo: acme/app @ main', 'pull request: #23', 'max cost: $1', 'profiles: native-codex', in that order and nothing else.
[unit] Table-driven: preview on a resolved repo with provider 'gitlab' throws ToolInputError with reason 'fix is GitHub-only' for a FIX and 'review is GitHub-only' for a REVIEW.
[unit] preview for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'REVIEW', prNumber: 23, feature: 'x', maxCostUsd: 1 } throws ToolInputError with reason 'feature is derived for REVIEW'.
[unit] preview for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'REVIEW', prNumber: 23, ref: 'dev', maxCostUsd: 1 } throws ToolInputError with reason 'ref is the default branch for REVIEW'.
[unit] preview for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'login', prNumber: 23, maxCostUsd: 1 } throws ToolInputError with reason 'prNumber is only for REVIEW and FIX'.

[unit] execute for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'FIX', prNumber: 23, maxCostUsd: 1, profiles: ['native-codex'] } calls FleetJobsService.dispatch with a DTO deep-equal to { repoId: <resolved repo id>, command: 'FIX', prNumber: 23, maxCostUsd: 1, profiles: ['native-codex'] }.

[integration] On the real test database, a koda_dispatch_job call { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'FIX', prNumber: 7023, maxCostUsd: 1 } posted to POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_dispatch_job?leaseEpoch=1 by the runner holding the thread job stores an action whose preview's third line is 'pull request: #7023'.
[integration] After that call and before any decision, no FleetJob with feature review-pr-7023 exists.
[integration] After the developer approves that action through POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions, exactly one FleetJob with feature review-pr-7023 exists.
[integration] That job's command is FIX.
[integration] That job's requestedById is the developer's id.
[integration] When REVIEW or FIX targets a resolved project repo with provider 'gitlab' through the runner tool route, the count of stored actions for that jobId/toolCallId is zero.

[unit] preview for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'PLAN', feature: 'add-auth', planFrom: 'docs/spec.md', maxCostUsd: 0.5 } in project web with default branch trunk returns exactly the lines 'Dispatch PLAN in web:', 'repo: acme/app @ trunk', 'feature: add-auth', 'max cost: $0.5', 'plan from: docs/spec.md', preserving the existing PLAN preview and line order.

[unit] execute for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5 } calls FleetJobsService.dispatch with a DTO deep-equal to { repoId: <resolved repo id>, command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5 }, preserving the existing RUN DTO with no prNumber key.
[unit] preview for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'FIX', prNumber: 23, feature: 'x', maxCostUsd: 1 } on a GitHub repo throws ToolInputError with reason 'feature is derived for FIX'.

routing.reasoning: Preview and DTO branches reuse an existing tool and complete HTTP/approval fixture harness without new abstractions; strict TDD remains required because the route-to-approval test exercises runner access, fencing and requester identity.

userStories.title: Dispatch REVIEW and FIX from CLI flags
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add CLI PR dispatch options, exact PR payload construction and canonical active-job conflict lookup.

**Motivation** — The K3 design goal 1 says a `FIX` can be dispatched "from REST, CLI, MCP and web (agent-first: no surface special-cased)", and §D7 notes K1 shipped `REVIEW` without a CLI flag.

**Approach** — `koda fleet dispatch` gains `--review <pr>` and `--fix <pr>`, each parsed with the existing `parsePositiveInt` (a malformed value fails inside commander with exit 1, as `--max-cost` does today). `--feature` changes from a required option to an optional one. The narrow `DispatchRunBody` type (`feature: string`) and its "only ever sends PLAN or RUN" comment go; `explainConflict` takes the lookup feature as an argument. A 409 on a `REVIEW` or `FIX` dispatch looks up the active job with feature `review-pr-<n>` (REVIEW and FIX of one PR share that feature, so the active job may be either kind) and prints the existing conflict message with that feature.

One field, two commands, every surface. `REVIEW` and `FIX` take a `prNumber` (an integer from 1 to 2147483647, the DTO's bounds) and no `feature`, `ref`, `planFrom`, `ticketRefs` or non-`raw` `bashMode`; the server derives the feature `review-pr-<prNumber>` and checks out the default branch (`normalizeDispatch`, unchanged), and refuses a non-GitHub repo (`FleetJobsService.dispatch`, reason `review is GitHub-only` / `fix is GitHub-only`). Each surface sends `{ repoId, command, prNumber, maxCostUsd }` plus the optional `profiles` and placement fields, and nothing else.

DispatchOptions gains `review?: number` and `fix?: number`, `feature?: string`. Use the existing generated DispatchFleetJobDto without editing generated code. Keep RUN/PLAN bodies, placement flags, output, JSON and API-error fallback unchanged. The three ordered semantic exit-3 checks belong to US-005; existing bashFlagProblem, label/pin, repo and runner checks still follow them in the final command. Do not add a CLI 32-bit upper-bound validator: parsePositiveInt accepts positive safe integers above 2147483647, and the API reports 400/exit 1.

**Scope** — In: options, numeric parsing, PR body, existing RUN body preservation and 409 feature/message/exit behavior. Out: the three ordered semantic validation branches (US-005), generated client changes, job show/list display and deployment-document examples. CLI: rejecting `--review`/`--fix` values above 2147483647 on the client: `parsePositiveInt` accepts them and the API answers 400, which the CLI reports as an API error (exit 1). CLI: exit code 3 for a malformed `--review`/`--fix` value: commander's option parser exits 1, as it already does for `--max-cost`. Choosing the pull request from a list of open pull requests on the web form or the CLI: the number is typed.

**Interface** — `DispatchOptions` gains `review?: number` and `fix?: number`, `feature?: string`; `findActiveJob(slug, repoId, feature)` remains unchanged; `explainConflict` takes the lookup feature as an argument.

[cli] koda fleet dispatch --repo acme/app --feature login --max-cost 1 sends a body deep-equal to { repoId: 'fr1', command: 'RUN', feature: 'login', maxCostUsd: 1 }.
[cli] koda fleet dispatch --repo acme/app --fix 0 --max-cost 1 rejects with a commander error whose code is commander.invalidArgument (the test program uses exitOverride).
[cli] koda fleet dispatch --repo acme/app --fix 0 --max-cost 1 makes no fleetJobsControllerDispatch call.

routing.reasoning: Extends one Commander command using existing parsers, generated services and conflict helpers; no new endpoint or domain abstraction.

userStories.title: Reject incompatible CLI PR dispatch flags before requests
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the ordered CLI semantic validations for mutually exclusive PR commands and RUN/PLAN-only flags.

**Motivation** — Today an agent in a koda thread or over MCP cannot ask for a review or a fix (the tool's `command` enum is `RUN` and `PLAN`), a CLI user cannot either (`--feature` is required and there is no PR flag), and a person reading a finished review on the web has no way to act on it except by hand.

**Approach** — Before any request, these validation failures exit 3 through the command's existing `invalid()` helper, in this order:
- `--review` and `--fix` together: `Use --review or --fix, not both`.
- `--review` or `--fix` with any of `--feature`, `--plan`, `--ref`, `--ticket`, `--bash-mode` or `--approval-timeout`: `--feature, --plan, --ref, --ticket, --bash-mode and --approval-timeout are not for --review or --fix`.
- Neither `--review` nor `--fix`, and no `--feature`: `--feature is required unless --review or --fix is given`.
After those, the existing checks run unchanged (`bashFlagProblem`, `--label` with `--pin`, unknown repo, unknown runner).

Extend fleet-dispatch.ts from US-004 and add fleet-dispatch-pr-validation.spec.ts, using the upstream PR command spec's mocks and program setup as a pattern. Make a fresh Commander program for each test case because option values persist across parseAsync calls. Explicit flags, including --bash-mode raw and --approval-timeout, count as incompatible; default empty ticket arrays do not. Numeric parse errors still belong to commander with exit 1, not invalid().

**Scope** — In: three ordered invalid() branches, messages, exit 3 and no-request behavior. Out: PR flag registration, body construction, malformed numeric parser behavior and conflict lookup (US-004).

**Interface** — `invalid(message)` remains the command's existing helper; `DispatchOptions` is the optional-feature/review/fix interface introduced by US-004.

userStories.title: Validate and serialize web PR dispatch forms
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the shared web dispatch schema and body type for PR commands while ignoring stale hidden RUN/PLAN values.

**Motivation** — K3-A shipped the `FIX` job kind and K3-B1 (PR #365) the follow-up review after a pushed fix, both live-checked (§9.155, §9.156) only through `curl` against the REST route.

**Approach** — Web PR number format. The form's `prNumber` is text. It is accepted when, after trimming, it matches `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and its value is at most 2147483647; `' 23 '` is accepted, `'023'`, `'+5'`, `'1e3'`, `'0'` and `''` are not. Everywhere the value is used it is `Number(trimmed)`, so the body, the 409 lookup feature and the prefill agree with the server's `review-pr-<n>`.

Web form library: schema, body, lookup feature. `buildDispatchSchema` accepts `command` `RUN`, `PLAN`, `REVIEW` or `FIX` and a new optional text field `prNumber`. For `RUN` and `PLAN` every existing check applies unchanged, and an empty `feature` still yields `fleet.dispatch.validation.feature`. For `REVIEW` and `FIX` the schema checks `prNumber` (call 5; otherwise the issue `fleet.dispatch.validation.prNumber` on path `prNumber`) and does not check `feature`, `ref`, `planFrom`, `ticketRefs`, `bashMode` or `approvalTimeoutMinutes`: those fields are hidden for the PR commands and keep stale values (`keepValuesOnUnmount`), so a stale invalid value must not block the submit. `repoId`, `profiles`, `maxCostUsd`, `selectorLabels` and the pin keep their checks for every command. Mechanism: zod runs field-level checks before the object's `superRefine` regardless of `command`, so the field schemas of `feature` (`.regex(FEATURE_RE)` and the `..` refine), `ref` (`.max(255)`), `planFrom` (`.max(512)`) and `ticketRefs` (`.max(MAX_DISPATCH_TICKETS)` and the `TICKET_REF_RE` refine) become lenient (`z.string()` / `z.string().optional()` / `z.array(z.string())`), and each of those checks moves into `superRefine` under `command === 'RUN' || command === 'PLAN'`, adding the same message on the same path with `ctx.addIssue`. The existing `approvalTimeoutMinutes` guard already follows this pattern.
`DISPATCH_DEFAULTS.prNumber` is `''`. `toDispatchBody` for `REVIEW`/`FIX` returns `{ repoId, command, prNumber: Number(trimmed prNumber), maxCostUsd }` plus `profiles` and the placement field when set, and never `feature`, `ref`, `planFrom`, `ticketRefs`, `bashMode`, `approvalTimeoutSec` or `acknowledgeOpenPr`. The `DispatchBody` type's `command` becomes the four-kind union, and it gains `prNumber?: number` with `feature` optional.

The RUN/PLAN results are unchanged, so the existing dispatch library spec's assertions keep holding (an empty feature on a RUN still yields fleet.dispatch.validation.feature). Reuse valid() and messages() patterns in the new PR library spec. The lookup-feature helper described alongside these changes is implemented by US-007, not this story.

**Scope** — In: buildDispatchSchema, defaults, toDispatchBody, DispatchBody and exact omission of hidden fields. Out: dispatchFeatureOf/query prefill/notice (US-007), page rendering/locales (US-009), mounted submit/conflict behavior (US-010). Do not clear hidden fields on command change.

**Interface** — `DispatchBody.command: 'RUN' | 'PLAN' | 'REVIEW' | 'FIX'`; `feature?: string`; `prNumber?: number`; `toDispatchBody(v: DispatchFormValues, opts: { acknowledgeOpenPr?: boolean } = {}): DispatchBody`.

userStories.title: Normalize PR query prefill, notice and conflict feature
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add safe PR/profile query prefill, the review notice discriminator and canonical dispatch feature lookup.

**Motivation** — Today an agent in a koda thread or over MCP cannot ask for a review or a fix (the tool's `command` enum is `RUN` and `PLAN`), a CLI user cannot either (`--feature` is required and there is no PR flag), and a person reading a finished review on the web has no way to act on it except by hand.

**Approach** — `dispatchPrefillFromQuery` accepts `command` `REVIEW` and `FIX`, a `prNumber` query (kept as `String(Number(trimmed))` only when it passes call 5 and the query's `command` is `REVIEW` or `FIX`) and a `profiles` query (one value or an array; each kept only when it matches `PROFILE_NAME_RE` and does not start with `RESERVED_PROFILE_PREFIX`, duplicates dropped, at most `MAX_PROFILES` kept). `DispatchQuery` gains `prNumber?: unknown` and `profiles?: unknown`. `prefillNotice` returns `'review'` when the prefill's `command` is `REVIEW` or `FIX`, before its existing rules, so its type is `'ticket' | 'plan' | 'review' | null`.

A new `dispatchFeatureOf(values)` returns `review-pr-<Number(trimmed prNumber)>` for `REVIEW`/`FIX` and the trimmed `feature` otherwise.

The form's `prNumber` is text. It is accepted when, after trimming, it matches `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and its value is at most 2147483647; `' 23 '` is accepted, `'023'`, `'+5'`, `'1e3'`, `'0'` and `''` are not. Everywhere the value is used it is `Number(trimmed)`, so the body, the 409 lookup feature and the prefill agree with the server's `review-pr-<n>`.

Existing prefill assertions keep holding because a query without prNumber or profiles yields the same result as today. Mirror ticketRefsFromQuery's scalar/array-query handling where relevant. Add fleet-dispatch-pr-prefill.spec.ts using the existing valid() pattern; keep filters and deduplication deterministic and do not change shared profile constants.

**Scope** — In: DispatchQuery, dispatchPrefillFromQuery, prefillNotice and dispatchFeatureOf. Out: schema/body (US-006), Fix-link helpers (US-008), page prefill rendering (US-009) and page 409 handling (US-010).

**Interface** — `dispatchFeatureOf(values: DispatchFormValues): string`; `prefillNotice` returns `'ticket' | 'plan' | 'review' | null`; `DispatchQuery` gains `prNumber?: unknown` and `profiles?: unknown`.

[unit] prefillNotice({ command: 'FIX', repoId: 'r1' }) returns 'review'.
[unit] dispatchFeatureOf returns 'review-pr-23' for command FIX with prNumber ' 23 '.
[unit] dispatchFeatureOf returns 'login' for command RUN with feature ' login '.

userStories.title: Derive permission-gated Fix action and dispatch query
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide pure helpers deciding Fix-action visibility and constructing its safe copied prefill query.

**Motivation** — Today an agent in a koda thread or over MCP cannot ask for a review or a fix (the tool's `command` enum is `RUN` and `PLAN`), a CLI user cannot either (`--feature` is required and there is no PR flag), and a person reading a finished review on the web has no way to act on it except by hand.

**Approach** — `lib/fleet-jobs.ts` gains `showFixAction(job, canDispatch): boolean` (true only for a `REVIEW` job in `COMPLETED` whose feature `reviewPrNumber` parses to at most 2147483647, when `canDispatch`) and `fixDispatchQuery(job): { command: 'FIX', repoId, prNumber, profiles? } | null` (`prNumber` the decimal string, `profiles` a new array copied from the job's profiles when non-empty, never the job's own array; `null` when the feature does not parse or exceeds 2147483647).

Use existing reviewPrNumber(feature), which validates canonical positive safe integers but is not itself restricted to 32 bits; enforce the extra maximum inside the new helpers without changing the existing reader's behavior. Carry only repo, pull request and optional profile chain, not cost or placement. Add fleet-jobs-fix-action.spec.ts for the pure helper outputs and array identity.

**Scope** — In: two new fleet-jobs helpers and permission/state/feature gates. Out: query parsing and notice (US-007), job-page rendering/locales (US-011), carrying review cost/placement, and a Review action on FIX jobs.

**Interface**
```typescript
showFixAction(job: Pick<FleetJobDto, 'command' | 'state' | 'feature'>, canDispatch: boolean): boolean
fixDispatchQuery(job: Pick<FleetJobDto, 'repoId' | 'feature' | 'profiles'>): { command: 'FIX'; repoId: string; prNumber: string; profiles?: string[] } | null
```

[unit] Table-driven: showFixAction returns false for that job with canDispatch false, with state FAILED, with command FIX, with feature login and with feature review-pr-2147483648.
[unit] fixDispatchQuery({ repoId: 'r1', feature: 'review-pr-23', profiles: ['native-codex'] }) returns { command: 'FIX', repoId: 'r1', prNumber: '23', profiles: ['native-codex'] }.
[unit] The profiles array fixDispatchQuery returns is not the same array object as the job's profiles.
[unit] fixDispatchQuery({ repoId: 'r1', feature: 'review-pr-23', profiles: [] }) returns { command: 'FIX', repoId: 'r1', prNumber: '23' }.
[unit] fixDispatchQuery returns null for feature login.

userStories.title: Render PR dispatch commands, input and prefilled notice
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the mounted web dispatch form with PR commands, conditional fields and review/profile prefill.

**Motivation** — Today an agent in a koda thread or over MCP cannot ask for a review or a fix (the tool's `command` enum is `RUN` and `PLAN`), a CLI user cannot either (`--feature` is required and there is no PR flag), and a person reading a finished review on the web has no way to act on it except by hand.

**Approach** — Web dispatch page. The command select lists `RUN`, `PLAN`, `REVIEW` (label `fleet.dispatch.commandReview`) and `FIX` (label `fleet.dispatch.commandFix`). For `REVIEW` and `FIX` the page shows a pull request number input (`data-testid="dispatch-pr-number"`, label `fleet.dispatch.prNumber`, hint `fleet.dispatch.prNumberHint`) and hides the ref, feature, spec path and tickets fields. Hiding wraps each existing `FormField` in a `<template v-if>` and leaves the `FormField` tags as they are. The bash fields are already `RUN`-only. The prefill applies `prNumber` and `profiles` from the query. The page's `prefilled` ref widens to `'ticket' | 'plan' | 'review' | null`, and the notice reads `prefilled === 'review' ? t('fleet.dispatch.prefilledReview') : prefilled === 'ticket' ? t('fleet.dispatch.prefilledTicket') : t('fleet.dispatch.prefilled')`.

Create fleet-dispatch-pr-page.spec.ts. Update only the C9 notice expectation in fleet-dispatch-page.spec.ts to the new review-first expression; its tickets FormField regex must keep holding because the field is wrapped, not edited. Keep all other source assertions, keepValuesOnUnmount, existing permission gate, placement controls and cost input. Do not hide PR commands based on repo provider or clear hidden values.

**Scope** — In: rendered options, text PR input, hidden RUN/PLAN fields, query application, review notice and six keys in both locales. Out: mounted submit/empty-PR/conflict behavior and dispatchFeatureOf lookup wiring (US-010), job-page Fix action/key (US-011). Hiding the web `Fix` action or the PR commands for a non-GitHub repo: the API refuses the dispatch with 422 and the form shows the API message. Choosing the pull request from a list of open pull requests on the web form or the CLI: the number is typed. Clearing the hidden RUN/PLAN form fields when the command changes: they keep their values and are simply not checked or sent for `REVIEW`/`FIX`.

userStories.title: Submit web PR dispatches and resolve active-job conflicts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Connect the mounted PR form to dispatch, block empty PR numbers and resolve 409 conflicts by canonical PR feature.

**Motivation** — K3-A shipped the `FIX` job kind and K3-B1 (PR #365) the follow-up review after a pushed fix, both live-checked (§9.155, §9.156) only through `curl` against the REST route.

**Approach** — A 409 looks up the active job with `jobsApi.findActiveJob(formValues.repoId, dispatchFeatureOf(formValues))`; the ticket open-PR confirmation stays `RUN`-only.

A new `dispatchFeatureOf(values)` returns `review-pr-<Number(trimmed prNumber)>` for `REVIEW`/`FIX` and the trimmed `feature` otherwise. Consume the helper from US-007, do not independently format a feature or send it in the PR body. Use the existing handleSubmit/buildDispatchSchema/toDispatchBody pipeline from US-006/US-009 for actual submit and empty-number blocking.

userStories.title: Offer Fix dispatch from completed REVIEW jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the permission-gated Fix link beside Dispatch run on completed REVIEW job pages.

**Motivation** — Today an agent in a koda thread or over MCP cannot ask for a review or a fix (the tool's `command` enum is `RUN` and `PLAN`), a CLI user cannot either (`--feature` is required and there is no PR flag), and a person reading a finished review on the web has no way to act on it except by hand.

**Approach** — Web `Fix` action. The job page renders a `NuxtLink` (`data-testid="fleet-job-dispatch-fix"`, text `fleet.jobs.actions.dispatchFix`) to `{ path: '/<slug>/fleet/dispatch', query: fixDispatchQuery(job) }` when `showFixAction(job, viewer.canDispatch)`, next to the existing `Dispatch run` link. The cost cap is not carried: the person sets it on the form.

New keys in both `en.json` and `zh.json`; the existing `used-keys-exist` spec requires every literal `t('...')` key to exist, and the fleet locale parity spec keeps the locales aligned. Job page: `fleet.jobs.actions.dispatchFix`.

Reuse viewer.canDispatch, which is already derived from the fleet.job.dispatch key. The only prefill is repo, PR and copied profiles: no cost or placement, no direct API dispatch on click. Leave existing Dispatch run, job headers, fixOutcome display and existing actions unchanged.

Out: pure helper implementation (US-008), dispatch-page behavior (US-009/US-010). A `Review` action on a `FIX` job page, or a `Fix` action on a `REVIEW` job that is not `COMPLETED`: a follow-up review already runs after a pushed fix (K3-B1). Carrying the review job's placement (labels, pinned runner) into the prefilled `Fix` dispatch: only repo, pull request and profiles are prefilled. outOfScope: Any API route, DTO, permission key, approval policy or audit change: the dispatch route already accepts `REVIEW` and `FIX`.
A CLI flag or web field for the cost cap of a `Fix` action prefilled from a review: the person or agent sets `maxCostUsd` on every dispatch.
Carrying the review job's placement (labels, pinned runner) into the prefilled `Fix` dispatch: only repo, pull request and profiles are prefilled.
A `Review` action on a `FIX` job page, or a `Fix` action on a `REVIEW` job that is not `COMPLETED`: a follow-up review already runs after a pushed fix (K3-B1).
Hiding the web `Fix` action or the PR commands for a non-GitHub repo: the API refuses the dispatch with 422 and the form shows the API message.
Choosing the pull request from a list of open pull requests on the web form or the CLI: the number is typed.
Checking on the client that the pull request is open, belongs to the repo or is not from a fork: the runner's nax refuses those and the job fails with nax's reason.
CLI: rejecting `--review`/`--fix` values above 2147483647 on the client: `parsePositiveInt` accepts them and the API answers 400, which the CLI reports as an API error (exit 1).
CLI: exit code 3 for a malformed `--review`/`--fix` value: commander's option parser exits 1, as it already does for `--max-cost`.
CLI `koda fleet job show` and `job list` display of `fixOutcome`: the job page already shows it (K3-A); the CLI prints the API's fields as they are.
Regenerating the CLI client: the generated types already carry `REVIEW`, `FIX` and `prNumber`.
The assistant tool's `RUN`/`PLAN` behaviour, preview lines and refusal reasons: unchanged.
